misconceptions.claim: A tracer is used to see the shape of an organ.
misconceptions.correction: It shows how the organ works, by following where the tracer goes in the body.

summary: Radiopharmaceuticals are compounds that are used for medical imaging and therapeutics.
The process of attaching a radioactive substance is called tagging.

sections.title: Biological Effects of Ionizing Radiation

misconceptions.claim: The gray and the sievert are the same unit, so absorbed dose and equivalent dose are the same quantity.
misconceptions.correction: The gray measures absorbed energy per kilogram. The sievert measures biological effect and includes the radiation weighting factor, so 1 Gy of alpha radiation gives a much larger equivalent dose than 1 Gy of gamma radiation.

summary: The biological effects of ionizing radiation are due to two effects it has on cells: interference with cell reproduction, and destruction of cell function.
A radiation dose unit called the rad is defined in terms of the ionizing energy deposited per kilogram of tissue: 1 rad=0.01 J/kg.
The SI unit for radiation dose is the gray (Gy), which is defined to be 1 Gy = 1 J/kg = 100 rad.

authored_exercises.stem: What does the absorbed dose of radiation measure?
authored_exercises.answer: The energy deposited by ionizing radiation per unit mass of material.
solution: Radiation deposits energy as it passes through matter.
The absorbed dose is that energy divided by the mass.
It is measured in gray, where 1 Gy = 1 J/kg.

sections.title: Therapeutic Uses of Ionizing Radiation
objectives: Explain the concept of radiotherapy and list typical doses for cancer therapy.
Explain how radiotherapy is planned to deliver a high dose to a tumour while limiting the dose to healthy tissue.

misconceptions.claim: The dose from a tracer is the same however the tracer is given.
misconceptions.correction: It depends on the activity, the half life, and how long it stays in the body.

summary: Radiotherapy is the use of ionizing radiation to treat ailments, now limited to cancer therapy.
The sensitivity of cancer cells to radiation enhances the ratio of cancer cells killed to normal cells killed, which is called the therapeutic ratio.
Doses for various organs are limited by the tolerance of normal tissue for radiation. Treatment is localized in one region of the body and spread out in time.
sections.no_worked_example_reason: The source section on Therapeutic Uses of Ionizing Radiation has no worked example; the teaching text derives the key results and the practice set applies them.

sections.title: Food Irradiation
objectives: Define food irradiation low dose, and free radicals.
Explain why irradiated food does not become radioactive.
Describe the effects of ionizing radiation on microorganisms and on food quality.

misconceptions.claim: Food that has been irradiated becomes radioactive.
misconceptions.correction: Irradiation does not make food radioactive any more than an X-ray makes a patient radioactive. The radiation passes through and is not retained.

summary: Food irradiation is the treatment of food with ionizing radiation.
Irradiating food can destroy insects and bacteria by creating free radicals and radiolytic products that can break apart cell membranes.
Food irradiation has produced no observable negative short-term effects for humans, but its long-term effects are unknown.
sections.no_worked_example_reason: The source carries no worked example for this section and no solved exercise to promote, so the practice is left to the exercises themselves.

authored_exercises.answer: The exposure of food to a controlled dose of ionizing radiation to kill microorganisms and insects or to slow spoilage.
solution: Ionizing radiation damages the DNA of microorganisms.
The food itself is not made radioactive.
The treatment can extend shelf life and reduce foodborne illness.

authored_exercises.stem: Does irradiated food become radioactive? Explain briefly.
authored_exercises.answer: No. The radiation passes through the food and is not retained; the food contains no induced radioactivity.
solution: Irradiation uses gamma rays, x-rays or electron beams.
These do not leave radioactive material behind.
The same is true of a patient who has had an X-ray.

authored_exercises.stem: Why is a high dose of radiation more damaging to rapidly dividing cells such as bacteria than to many mature food cells?
authored_exercises.answer: Rapidly dividing cells are more sensitive to DNA damage because they are actively copying and repairing DNA.
solution: Ionizing radiation damages DNA.
Cells that divide often have less time to repair the damage.
Microorganisms and insect cells are therefore hit harder than the bulk of the food tissue.

sections.no_exam_link_reason: Food irradiation is an applied extension and is not named in either syllabus.

sections.title: Fusion
objectives: Discuss processes to achieve practical fusion energy generation.

misconceptions.claim: Nuclear fusion is the splitting of a heavy nucleus into lighter ones.
misconceptions.correction: Fusion joins light nuclei into a heavier one. Fission splits a heavy nucleus. Both release energy when the binding energy per nucleon increases.

summary: Nuclear fusion is a reaction in which two nuclei are combined to form a larger nucleus. It releases energy when light nuclei are fused to form medium-mass nuclei.

Fusion is the source of energy in stars, with the proton-proton cycle, 1H +1H →2H+e++ve (0.42 MeV)1H+2H→3He +γ (5.49 MeV)3He +3He→4He+1H+1H (12.86 MeV) being the principal sequence of energy-producing reactions in our Sun.
The overall effect of the proton-proton cycle is 2e−+41H→4He+2ve+6γ (26.7 MeV),where the 26.7 MeV includes the energy of the positrons emitted and annihilated.

sections.title: Fission
objectives: Discuss how fission fuel reacts and describe what it produces.
Describe controlled and uncontrolled chain reactions.

misconceptions.claim: A nuclear power reactor can explode like a nuclear bomb.
misconceptions.correction: A power reactor cannot produce a nuclear explosion because its fuel is not highly enriched enough and its geometry is not designed for a runaway supercritical chain reaction. A reactor accident is a different kind of event.

summary: Nuclear fission is a reaction in which a nucleus is split.
Fission releases energy when heavy nuclei are split into medium-mass nuclei.

Self-sustained fission is possible, because neutron-induced fission also produces neutrons that can induce other fissions, n+AX→FF1+FF2+xn, where FF1 and FF2 are the two daughter nuclei, or fission fragments, and x is the number of neutrons produced.

sections.title: Nuclear Weapons
objectives: Discuss different types of fission and thermonuclear bombs.
Explain the ill effects of nuclear explosion.

misconceptions.claim: A nuclear weapon releases its energy by chemical burning of the fissile material.
misconceptions.correction: The energy comes from nuclear fission or fusion, where a small mass defect is converted to energy through E = mc². Chemical burning involves only electron rearrangements and releases far less energy per kilogram.

summary: There are two types of nuclear weapons—fission bombs use fission alone, whereas thermonuclear bombs use fission to ignite fusion.
Both types of weapons produce huge numbers of nuclear reactions in a very short time.
Energy yields are measured in kilotons or megatons of equivalent conventional explosives and range from 0.1 kT to more than 20 MT.

(b) This result is about 6 MeV greater than the result for spontaneous fission. Why? (c) Confirm that the total number of nucleons and total charge are conserved in this reaction.

sec-6:exr-75.answer: 20.58 MeV and 2.22 MeV. ${}^{4}He$ is more tightly bound: about 5.15 MeV per nucleon, compared with about 1.11 MeV per nucleon for ${}^{2}H$.

sec-2:exr-34.stem: A brain scan uses 7.50 mCi of ${}^{99m}\mathrm{Tc}$. The half-life of ${}^{99m}\mathrm{Tc}$ is 6.01 h. What mass of technetium is present?
solution: Convert the activity: $A=(7.50\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{Ci})(3.70\times10^{10}\ \mathrm{Bq/Ci})=2.78\times10^{8}\ \mathrm{Bq}$.
The decay constant is $\lambda=\ln 2/T_{1/2}=0.693/(6.01\times3600\ \mathrm{s})=3.20\times10^{-5}\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$.
The number of nuclei is $N=A/\lambda=(2.78\times10^{8})/(3.20\times10^{-5})=8.67\times10^{12}$.
The mass is $m=(N/N_{A})M=(8.67\times10^{12}/6.02\times10^{23})(99\ \mathrm{g/mol})=1.43\times10^{-9}\ \mathrm{g}$.
